description: A complete, self-contained inverse-dynamics pipeline. It generates its own marker data from a known pose, then runs IK, ID and static optimization, so it needs nothing but a network connection for the model. Run with: python scripts/run_spec.py template/self-contained-pipeline.json
note: Because the markers are synthesised from a pose of the model itself, IK should recover that pose almost exactly. That makes this a good end-to-end check that the whole chain works before you point it at real capture data. The model is arm26 (2 coordinates, 6 muscles, 3 markers) - deliberately small so the run takes seconds. Note that the registry's gait models ship WITHOUT a marker set, so they cannot drive IK; supply your own marker file and a marked-up model for gait work.

args.source:
import opensim as osim
osim.Logger.setLevelString('Error')

# A held pose over 0.5 s. The frame count matters: inverse dynamics needs enough
# samples to differentiate the motion, and a handful will fail in the spline
# fit rather than give a useful answer.
POSE = {'r_shoulder_elev': 0.5, 'r_elbow_flex': 1.0}
FRAMES, DT = 51, 0.01
out = Path('opensim_results'); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

model = osim.Model(str(resolve_model('arm26')))
state = model.initSystem()
coords = model.getCoordinateSet()
for name, value in POSE.items():
    coords.get(name).setValue(state, float(value))
model.realizePosition(state)

markers = model.getMarkerSet()
names = [markers.get(i).getName() for i in range(markers.getSize())]
print('markers on this model:', names)

table = osim.TimeSeriesTableVec3()
labels = osim.StdVectorString()
for n in names:
    labels.append(n)
table.setColumnLabels(labels)
for f in range(FRAMES):
    row = osim.RowVectorVec3(len(names))
    for i in range(len(names)):
        row.__setitem__(i, markers.get(i).getLocationInGround(state))
    table.appendRow(f * DT, row)

# The TRC writer requires the header keys a real capture file carries.
for k, v in (('DataRate','100'), ('CameraRate','100'), ('NumFrames',str(FRAMES)),
             ('NumMarkers', str(len(names))), ('Units','m'), ('OrigDataRate','100'),
             ('OrigDataStartFrame','1'), ('OrigNumFrames',str(FRAMES))):
    table.addTableMetaDataString(k, v)
osim.TRCFileAdapter().write(table, str(out / 'posed.trc'))
print('wrote', out / 'posed.trc', 'with', FRAMES, 'frames')
